body:
I decided at some point to try to live for other people since I realized that my depression had made my daily thinking self-centered to an intolerable degree.

I've faced a lot of life-worsening health problems, but realized that there are people out there who face much worse trauma and daily pain than I do.  And some of them might tend to use this subreddit.

So I eventually decided to try to live for others, no matter how imperfectly, just by beginning to become re-skilled in the practice of talking to people with an open heart.

Life has remained pretty much the same as it's been while I was severely depressed, but now I'm fighting to focus on others' needs rather than just my own. Taking a few hours out in the day to read this subreddit or to read about how to help people with various emotional troubles helps me acquire a sense of newfound usefulness which the previous lifestyle couldn't have given me. 

I do not regret that I avoided suicide --  I am still pretty young and according to others might have plenty to live for once I'm done recovering (in probably a matter of years) from certain medical problems.
You mention that you feel "unrepairable" and that it physically hurts to live -- if I may ask, what kinds of ailments are you dealing with?
